note: Provisional candidates only; canon is never minted here. The implementation audit must census the existing catalog and adjudicate exact IDs.

census.canon_estimate: ~732 command ids across 56 families at the 2026-08-08 packet window

retire_or_alias.reason: Old chip/bloom architecture is superseded by destination + record navigation; keep a compatibility alias only if telemetry shows live callers.

supersede_into_family.note: Standalone per-manager openers collapse into one navigation family. In c4 this id resolves to a cross-concept receipt (c2 owns the surface).
This concept's OWN navigation overlap: c4 renders Storage & Retention natively, and the deep link #/manager/manager.storage is the canonical route — the bespoke opener supersedes into the family.

merge_flag.note: Same operation; keep cmd.settings.reset.apply with a scope payload (category|all) and retire the category-specific id.

reuse_flag.note: Theme apply/preview commands already exist; the settings surface must reuse them, not mint settings-local theme commands.
Reuse for opening the Actions manager destination; operational panel commands stay in their own family.

new_candidates.distinguishes: Persistent retention policy change per data class; distinct from the one-shot compaction/cleanup actions and from status projections.
The 'Back Up Now' action with kind payload (settings|project); leaves a restore point + receipt. Distinct from cmd.settings.export (portable file) and from the schedule setting.
Restore from a named restore point: preview, fresh pre-restore point, atomic apply, receipt.
Scratch-dataset restore with hash verification; never touches live data — a different permission class than restore.
Exports an artifact out of the vault with redaction rules applied on the way out.
Applies staged redaction rules; original stays sealed. Distinct from export.
Deletes a retention-expired artifact after confirmation; receipt survives the artifact.
Removes a checkout, never a branch; hard-fails on leased worktrees (lease is validated in the command, not the UI).
Pinning is settings-owned readiness curation; run operations stay in the panel's own family.
Re-fetches readiness + latest runs; honestly unavailable offline (typed error, not a silent no-op).
Add-registry flow with certificate-chain validation; cert warnings pause with trust guidance instead of failing.
Reorders provider fallback per kind (search/crawl/fetch); distinct from enabling/setup.
Phased operation (scanning/indexing/ready) with failure records; distinct from the enable setting and the clear-cache action.
Report-only by contract: typed result (wouldFree, skipped-with-reasons, receipt); can never delete.
The destructive half; requires a current dry-run reference and explicit confirmation; leases and legal holds are command-level exclusions.
